about: Names people type for one enzyme, curated by hand. Each row reads one name as ONE EC number (and, where it is one protein of that EC, the isoform), and says where that reading comes from. Every EC is checked against the committed IUBMB nomenclature index by caterva/tests/test_names_people_type.py. 'organism' is the organism assumed when none was given: 'always' rows (a viral protease) assume it whatever was typed; 'uppercase' rows only when the name was typed as a human gene symbol is written (CYP2B6, not Cyp2b10). 'organisms' (when present) lists the organisms a row is read for when an organism is given: CYP2B6 is a human gene and is not read for mouse, IDH1 is not read for yeast, where it is the NAD-dependent subunit. 'by_organism' rows (PEPCK) mean different enzymes in different organisms and are read only when the organism is known. 'rows_must_name_it' rows are one protein of an EC number that holds many distinct proteins (KPC-2 among the beta-lactamases, ERK2 among the MAP kinases): a BRENDA row is taken as measuring it only when the row's UniProt accession is one of 'accessions' or its commentary names it (by 'names', the isoform or 'row_names'); caterva/compose/protein_rows.py withholds any other.
